title: Large Language Models Struggle to Describe the Haystack without Human Help: A Social Science-Inspired Evaluation of Topic Models
subcategory: user study of LDA vs LLM topic tools for data exploration
task: Measuring what users learn from topic models and LLM-based tools
problem: LLM-based topic tools are replacing probabilistic models for content analysis without evidence that they help users understand a corpus.
architecture: Pre-test/post-test user study (120 Prolific users, 15 per condition and dataset) comparing LDA, TopicGPT (GPT-4, Mistral-7B, LLaMA-2-70B variants), LLooM and BASS (Bot-Assisted Semantic Search: LLM-suggested topics refined by users with active learning); clustering metrics, automatic answer metrics and Bradley-Terry preferences.

datasets.name: Sci-Fi
datasets.details: documents generated from predefined question-answer pairs

key_results: Bills: BASS ARI 0.45 and NMI 0.54 vs LDA 0.27 and 0.47 and TopicGPT 0.23 and 0.42.
Sci-Fi: TopicGPT finds only 4 topics with NMI 0.18 vs LDA 0.56 and BASS 0.69.
Users approved BASS-suggested topics 93% of the time on Bills vs 62% on Sci-Fi.
strengths: Measures knowledge gained by real users rather than topic-word metrics.
Shows unsupervised LLM topics are overly generic on domain-specific data.

limitations.text: User studies are hard to scale; BASS needs considerable human effort and has no clear stopping criterion.
Two datasets, one of them synthetic; 15 users per condition.
